EMOTIONAL INTELLIGENCE / LEVEL I

Emotional Intelligence Trainer Training · Level I

Beijing, 11–16 August 2026. Six days of experiential learning, from emotional awareness and communication to designing and facilitating activities.

LEARNING BY EXPERIENCE

Experience the work before facilitating it

Emotional intelligence education goes beyond learning concepts. Michel's course invites participants to listen, express themselves, cooperate and exchange feedback, while examining why activities are structured as they are and how facilitators respond to the group. Personal experience and program design develop together.

The Beijing 2026 course has concluded. Its actual themes and classroom scenes below trace the learning journey.

BEIJING · AUGUST 2026

SIX DAYS IN BEIJING

A six-day learning journey

Each day combines personal experience with observation and reflection on teaching methods.

DAY 01

Connection and trust

Use welcoming activities, shared agreements and cooperative exercises to create room for expression and exploration.

DAY 02

Communication and responsibility

Practise listening, asking and responding; notice how communication shapes choices and relationships.

DAY 03

Self-awareness and recognizing emotion

Start with bodily reactions and everyday experience to recognize emotions and express feelings clearly.

DAY 04

Strengths, feedback and collective wisdom

Discover personal strengths through peer feedback and explore how different experiences can support one another.

DAY 05

Cooperation, consensus and integration

Explore cooperation and disagreement through group activities, bringing personal awareness into real group relationships.

DAY 06

Program design and reflection

Moving from learner to facilitator, participants define goals, sequence activities and plan reflection to shape a session of their own.

THE LEARNING ARC

From presence to relationships and action

The course places personal emotional skills and group facilitation on one learning path. Participants first notice their own experience, then practise understanding and working with others, before designing activities that invite others to learn.

Presence and self-awarenessRecognizing and regulating emotionsListening, communication and relationshipsCooperation and consensusActivity design and facilitation

INSIDE THE CLASSROOM

Inside the Beijing Level I classroom

From Michel's teaching to group practice, see how the approach unfolds in the classroom.

FROM CLASS TO PRACTICE

From learning to facilitation

In Beijing's November Level II course, participants turned their Level I experience into themed sessions: planning, facilitating, observing group dynamics and receiving feedback. The classroom became a starting point for continued peer learning.
